2\. No automatic restart when a handover's successor dies 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness 
start_after_alarm treats any trusted LEAD-STARTED newer than since as the stall's one start
(rule 2). On the ordinary path since is the last progress time, and cmd_handoff writes the step
before the outgoing lead runs start-lead, so the successor's LEAD-STARTED is always newer than
that progress. The result is that a successor whose start didn't take, or that joined and died
before its first step change or push, gets alarms and reminders but never the watchdog start. The
spec's per-path list ("released after a handover whose successor never came: one takeover or plain
start") and the CHANGELOG and ARCHITECT text all promise that start.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description On the ordinary-stall path, `start_after_alarm` counts the handover's own `LEAD-STARTED` (posted by role `lead` right after `handoff` writes the step) as the stall's one start. As a result, the watchdog never starts a lead when a handover's successor fails to join or dies before making progress. The spec says this path gets one start. ## Fix Focus Areas - room.py[3033-3037] - docs/design/m6d-watchdog.md[13-13] - tests/test_m6d.py[1-438] ## Recommended Fix Pick one of these and apply it everywhere: - **Change the code to match the spec:** in rule 2, count only `LEAD-STARTED`s that aren't the handover's. For example, count only role `watchdog`/`architect` starts, or only starts newer than the first alarm of the stall. Then a lead-role `LEAD-STARTED` posted before the alarm doesn't use up the one start. - **Change the docs to match the code:** remove the claim from the spec's per-path list, the CHANGELOG and ARCHITECT.md.
